limitations: This parent supplies procedural framing without projecting any unselected stage body.
The legality-stage boundary remains material even though it is outside the parent's cited proposal and cost ranges.
No stack proposal, legal-permission decision, casting step, or rollback operation is implemented.
rules.paraphrase: Casting takes a spell, card, or copy from its former location to the stack and requires its costs to be paid through an ordered procedure. The proposal and cost stages form parts of that procedure; permission to begin and the ability to finish every required step legally constrain it. Failure to complete a required step calls for undoing the casting proposal under a separate rule.
rules.topic: Ordered casting procedure and incomplete stage coverage

limitations: The declarations are authored semantic evidence, with no mode, splice, variable, hybrid, or Phyrexian operation.
An alternative cost is a candidate base-cost replacement rather than a subtraction from the normal mana cost.
Referenced choice and cost families remain unresolved; no complete alternative-method interaction algorithm is supplied.
rules.paraphrase: The casting declaration records modes, splice use with chosen cards revealed from hand, alternative or additional costs, variable values, and applicable hybrid or Phyrexian payment choices. A variable whose value depends on a choice normally made later brings that choice into this stage. Earlier casting choices can constrain these declarations. Multiple alternative methods or multiple alternative costs cannot simply be combined for one spell; the later total-cost stage uses the declarations.
rules.topic: Casting declarations and constraints on cost choices

limitations: Cost composition and lock-in are descriptions; no amount is computed and no cost effect is applied.
No real Card text, cost-modification evaluator, layer runtime, or cost-locking runtime is supplied.
rules.paraphrase: The total starts with either the normal mana cost or the chosen alternative cost, then accounts for additional costs, increases, and reductions. The player chooses the sequence when several reductions apply, and the mana portion has a zero lower bound. Effects that directly change the resulting total are considered after those ordinary components. Once determined, the total is locked and later changes do not alter it.
rules.topic: Composition and lock-in of the total casting cost

limitations: The opportunity is represented without mana abilities, production, pools, activation, priority, or payment.
Fictional mana behavior supplies no authority for real rule 605.
rules.paraphrase: A total cost that requires a mana payment gives the casting player an opportunity to use mana abilities before paying that cost. The referenced mana-ability system remains outside the selected source scope.

limitations: Payment grouping and completeness requirements are represented without performing any payment.
No library inspection, randomization, sacrifice, tap, discard, life payment, or object movement is supplied.
Any example included in the verified source block contributes only to its hash and span; its prose is not retained.
rules.paraphrase: The payer handles ordinary components first, choosing their order within that group. Components involving randomness or moving library objects to a public zone belong to the remaining group and may be ordered within that group. Every required component must be payable and paid in full; a partial payment does not satisfy a cost.
rules.topic: Payment groups and all-or-nothing cost requirements
